findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector was unable to verify a certified food protection manager certification during today’s inspection. Education was carried out. Ensure that there is at least one certified food protection manager present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The coving tiles along the compartmental wall next to the fryers and on the right side of the walk-in cooler were observed broken and missing including a large tile under the fryers. PIC assured inspector that the tiles will be replaced. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done to maintain the facility in good repairs.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: The ventilation filters in hood system were observed with accumulated dust and soil. Education was carried out and PIC assured inspector that the filters will be cleaned. Ensure that the hood filters are cleaned to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed donning gloves without handwashing. PIC was made aware. Ensure that employees are aware and remember to wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The thermometers in the large display cooler at the deli were observed not functional. PIC was made aware. A few stem thermometer were placed for temporary use until hanging thermometer are installed. Ensure that thermometers are always present within the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of food debris under fryer and the oven at the deli. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that it was going to be cleaned. Ensure that staff are aware of the accumulation of food debris under equipment and closed surfaces hence, need to extend cleaning procedures to closed spaces as well. Ensure that closed spaces and surfaces under equipments are routinely monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Inspector observed a series of ready to eat food items such as salads, dressings, fruits, and other condiments not properly dated and marked as required in the second walk-in cooler at the deli department. Discussed with PIC and PIC instructed employees to immediately date mark the items on the shelves. Ensure that all food items such as the one mentioned are properly dated marked at all time for safety. 

(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

2. The hand siink in the meat department was observed leaking at the meat department cooling area.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.15  Inspector observed used mop water being stored in the mop bucket by the mop sink in the deli area. Discussed with PIC. The mop water was disposed properly. Ensure that used mop water are disposed appropriated to discourage the harborage of pest. 

Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11. Inspector observed multiple half used employee drinks and food being stored together with food items meant for sale. Discussed with PIC and the items belonging to employees were taken away to be stored properly. Discussion about designated storage for employees was held. Ensure that there is a designated area for employees to store their personal items at all time.

(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The hand-sink was observed to be obstructed by a food-tray cart when inspectors arrived at the facility. Discussed with PIC and the cart was removed to make the hand-sink accessible. Ensure that the hand sink is accessible at all time for use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed eggs being stored over mushrooms in the walk-in cooler in the meat department. PIC was made aware of the appropriate storage order for food items and the eggs were moved a shelf below the mushrooms in order to correct the storage order. Ensure that all food items are stored appropriately to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The open display cooler at the Sushi Kabar was observed to be out of temperature. PIC was made aware of the malfunction. The sushi in the cooler were probed and read at a temperature of 44F. The sushi in the cooler were moved to another cooler to enable the maintenance of the appropriate temperature. Ensure that cold holdings are often checked to ensure they maintain the adequate temperature to avoid food spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: There is observed a sanitizer bucket in the basin of the hand sink near the mop sink. The sanitizer bucket was removed from the basin of the hand sink. Ensure that the hand sink is utilized for no other purpose than hand washing. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink is observed to have a black tube present that drains into the basin of the hand sink. This tube is the draining water from the steam from the ovens. This tube needs to be redirected so that it drains into the mop sink so that the hand sink has no other purpose than hand washing. Ensure that hand sinks in the facility are utilized for no other purpose than hand washing.  
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: The walk-in cooler and single door freezer are observed without an internal thermometer separate from the manufacturer’s display. Ensure that internal hanging thermometers/temperature measuring devices separate from the manufacturer’s are present in each cold holding unit. 
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The tile floor in the deli kitchen is observed to be missing grout along the cook-line and near the mop sink and along the fryer station which is resulting in an accumulation of food debris/moisture. Ensure the flooring tiles and between them are cleaned, replaced if broken and re-grouted to create an easily cleanable surface that does not allow for the accumulation of moisture or food debris. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
